subject: Provide safe homes for Lisa, Mariama, and Max
emailBody:
Dear Councillor Nicholson,

I am a Hackney resident writing to express huge concern for the health and safety of Hackney Council tenants Lisa, Mariama, and Max.

Lisa, Mariama and Max have been tenants of the Hackney Council for years. They have experienced a series of serious disrepair issues, including severe damp and mould. This has had proven impacts on their health, and that of the children of Lisa and Mariama.

Lisa, Mariama and Max have raised these concerns with Hackney Council over the years, but there has been no appropriate action. 

The London Renters Union has requested that you meet them in order to discuss this situation for months. You have failed to respond. 

As a resident in Hackney, I am deeply concerned that the council is ignoring its tenants and constituents. The Hackney Labour Party’s attitude to residents in the borough shows a lack of concern for our living conditions and health. The Labour Party cannot take our votes for granted when Labour councillors repeatedly fail to treat our fellow Hackney residents with the dignity and care that we all deserve. 

It is particularly damning that this is happening just as Awaab’s Law has come into force. Awaab’s law states that social landlords have an absolute obligation to deal with serious health hazards in their tenants' homes. The solution to the issues should take the tenant’s health into account. If the issues can’t be resolved, the landlord should offer alternative accommodation. 

We demand that you urgently meet the London Renters Unions in order to discuss the situations of Lisa, Mariama, and Max, and that you take action to ensure that they and their families have the safe home that all residents need.

Kind regards,
 {{username}}

subject: Do not evict MZ
emailBody:
Dear Zoe,

I am writing to you as a member of the London Renters Union, with great concern for a tenant, MZ, who you are about to evict.

I understand you are evicting her based on unsubstantiated allegations, and rent arrears for which she had already set up a payment plan. This is unreasonable, unjust, and against your core values as a self-proclaimed 'tenant led' organisation.

Despite her very reasonable request for an extension to her stay until her homelessness assessment is carried out by the council, you have refused this. You have now offered to accommodate her but in another flat and only until the end of the month. This means she will still be at risk of homelessness and will be forced to move from her home today.

As an organisation that claims to 'help people affected by homelessness', you will undoubtedly be aware that a young woman like MZ faces an extremely high risk of harm should she become street homeless. I am also aware that this tenant is neurodivergent and it's clear this has not been taken into account in your decision to evict her.

I therefore urge you not to go ahead with her eviction and to engage with her and her support worker from Hackney Quest.


Yours sincerely,{{username}}

subject: Fix the disrepair at 11a Powell Road
emailBody:
Dear Juda Bash,

I am a member of the London Renters Union, a membership organisation of over 7,000 renters that takes action on housing issues through legal advocacy, media work and collective action.

I am writing in solidarity with our member Chinye Osai, who lives at 11a Powell Road, London E5 8DJ, where you act as letting agent.

On 28 July, London Renters Union wrote to you on Chinye's behalf setting out serious, ongoing disrepair at the property, including:

1. Black mould in the shared bathroom, in Chinye's bedroom (window sills) and wardrobe - made worse by a windowless, unventilated basement, and a serious risk to Chinye's respiratory health, which you have been made aware of on numerous occasions

2. A clogged, leaking kitchen drain causing floods and repeated failures of the communal washing machine

3. A clogged bathroom drain causing waste water and scum to pool in the bathtub

4. A broken door handle preventing Chinye from securing her room

5. A rodent hole in the communal kitchen fire door, which is also missing its intumescent strip and does not close properly against its frame. This is a serious fire safety failure, given the heightened fire risk in kitchens

6. A rodent hole in the back door, giving pests direct access to the kitchen and bin area

7. Water pressure insufficient to serve the property's five tenants when more than one outlet is in use

8. Inadequate emergency lighting in the basement hallway, leaving the corridor by Chinye's room in darkness. This was also observed by the London Fire Brigade on 28 June 2026

9. A neglected, unsafe backyard with loose tiles and rubbish

10. A hole in the internal wall by the front door

These issues were first reported to you up to three months ago, and again on 29 June, 16 July and 21 July 2026, plus an on-site surveyor visit on 3 July 2026. Chinye has received only two generic acknowledgements in response. No schedule, and no repairs.

We asked you to confirm a schedule of repairs within five working days. That deadline has now passed with no meaningful response.

Under Section 11 of the Landlord and Tenant Act 1985, you have an absolute, non-excludable obligation to keep this property in repair throughout the tenancy. Under the Homes (Fitness for Human Habitation) Act 2018, you must address conditions that risk a tenant's health and safety, which the mould and the non-compliant fire door plainly do.

I am one of thousands of London Renters Union members following this case, and I am asking you, alongside my fellow members, to act now. Please confirm a schedule for these repairs without further delay. If this is not resolved, London Renters Union will refer 11a Powell Road to Hackney Council's environmental health team and PRS team to seek an inspection and an Improvement Notice, and will consider further public action against Homelets Ltd. London Renters Union has a long history of successful public action, and reaches tens of thousands of followers across social media. We do not intend to stay quiet on this.

Yours sincerely,
{{username}}
